title: chat edge gate and spark2 fallback

targets.text: chat.culture.dev sits behind a Cloudflare Worker that gates traffic at the edge, so anonymous traffic never reaches our machines and a real outage page shows when both sparks are down; when spark fails, signed-in people land on spark2 instead of a 500, after signing in again if needed
A simulated spark failure with Worker and spark2 in place returns the app, not a 500, to a signed-in test account
On 2026-11-03 signed-in users got 500s from LensConnectionLost for up to 41h after the Nov 2 00:44 reboot, while anonymous GET / still returned 200, and nothing alerted anyone
The dates and durations match the journal: first refusal Nov 2 00:44, restored Nov 3 17:58
culture server start ignores a pidfile whose PID is not a culture process, so a reboot cannot wedge the IRCd; this ships before any failover work
With a pidfile pointing at another user's thread, culture server start succeeds; a test covers it
The lens exposes a readiness check that fails when its IRCd is unreachable; failover and alerting key on it, not on / or /healthz
With the IRCd stopped the readiness check returns non-200, and with it running returns 200
No per-request round-robin between instances: one person's session stays on one instance until that instance fails
Two requests from one session always reach the same instance while that instance is healthy
Tunnel replicas are not the fallback mechanism: each host gets its own tunnel and the Worker chooses between them
spark and spark2 connect through different tunnel UUIDs
A Worker on chat.culture.dev picks the origin, pins a session to it, fails over on origin failure, and serves a static outage page when both are down
Stopping both origins yields the static outage page, and the Worker stays within Free limits at current traffic
Origin hostnames accept only the Worker's credential and the lens trusts a verifiable identity from it, so anonymous traffic never reaches our machines
A direct request to an origin hostname without the Worker's credential is refused before reaching the lens
spark2 is provisioned with irc-lens config, cloudflared, its own secrets and a running IRCd, using the supported install verbs
culture console install and culture server install produce running units on spark2, reachable only through its tunnel
The service sends periodic pings to healthchecks.io using the grant secret CULTURE_HEALTHCHECK_URL, so an outage alerts even when our machines cannot send anything
Pings are sent only after a real IRCd readiness check passes, so a healthy landing page with a dead IRCd stops the pings
The check also alerts when the pinger's host is off, because silence alone turns it down
The owner receives an hourly email while any health check is down, until it recovers
With the check down for over an hour, at least 2 reminder emails arrive at the owner's address
After a reboot the standby rejoins the mesh without a person unlocking its keyring, because a locked keyring leaves spark2 with no link credentials
After a spark2 reboot with no human action, it links to at least one peer
The owner as operator, and approved people who use chat.culture.dev as their mesh console
Every behaviour in this spec is observable by one of these two groups
When spark fails, people reach spark2 after signing in again if needed, as spark2-<nick>; when both are down they see an outage page; the owner is told by email either way
Each clause is exercised in the failover drill: sign-in again, spark2 nick, outage page, email

An IRCd outage behind a healthy landing page alerts the owner within 10 minutes, against about 41 hours unnoticed on 2026-11-03; a simulated spark failure serves signed-in people from spark2 within 5 minutes
Both timings are measured in a drill, not estimated

spark2's standby lens holds a copy of accounts and permissions from spark's guests.db, one-way and refreshed on a schedule, because an empty store would refuse every approved person including the admin
After a copy, an approved person can sign in on spark2 and holds the same role and grants

The health ping ships as part of the culture app: a CLI verb installs the timer on any host, reads the check URL from grant and the site address from the lens config, replacing the hand-written script and units on spark

On a host with only the culture install and the grant secret, the CLI verb alone produces a timer that pings healthchecks.io, reports /fail when /readyz fails, and spark runs on it with the hand-written files removed
Browser POSTs work through the Worker: _origin_ok compares Origin to the request host, so a Worker fetching an origin hostname with a different Host gets every browser POST refused
A real browser signs in and sends a message through the Worker, on both origins
Health pings check the primary's own local /readyz as well as the public one, so a failover can't hide that spark is down: after failover the public /readyz would answer 200 from spark2
With spark's IRCd stopped and traffic on spark2, the check goes down and hourly reminders arrive
Failover trips only after several consecutive failed /readyz checks, and returning to spark is a deliberate step, so a routine restart can't bounce everyone onto a different nick
Restarting the console or IRCd during a deploy moves no one to spark2
The Worker can be removed in one step: deleting its route restores direct access through the existing tunnel, and that path stays available until the Worker has proven itself
A rehearsed rollback restores signed-in service within 5 minutes

The guests.db copy to spark2 stays private: it holds emails, password and token hashes, so it travels only over the tailnet or LAN, stays mode 0600 on spark2, and has the same retention as the original
After a copy, the file on spark2 is mode 0600 and no copy path crosses the public internet

tasks.summary: Record the reliability work as delivered: stale pidfile fix (culture#520, 14.13.2) and /readyz (irc-lens#91, 0.19.0)
acceptance_criteria: spark, spark2, thor and orin report culture 14.13.2, and spark reports irc-lens 0.19.0
Public /readyz returns 200 with Cache-Control no-store
Stopping a test IRCd makes /readyz return 503 in tests/test_readyz.py
tasks.instruction: Verification only, no code. Cite the merged PRs and test names. If a check fails, file a deviation.

tasks.summary: POST spike: prove a browser POST through a Worker on an in-zone test hostname reaches the lens with Origin accepted
acceptance_criteria: A POST through the Worker to a test route returns the lens's normal response, not the Origin-denied 403
The result records whether cf.resolveOverride keeps Host chat.culture.dev through the tunnel, or whether the lens needs a configured public origin
Visitor IP seen by the lens equals the client's IP, not a Cloudflare address, so client_ip rate limits still work
The test Worker and hostname are deleted afterwards
tasks.instruction: Extend the earlier scratch spike with a POST and a same-zone route. Owner runs the deploy, since auto mode blocks it. The result chooses t6's approach, so finish this first.

tasks.summary: culture: `culture console install --healthcheck` verb that installs the health ping timer on any host
acceptance_criteria: Files: culture_core/cli/console.py, a new culture_core/cli/shared/healthcheck.py, tests/test_console_healthcheck.py, docs/reference/cli/console.md
Generated unit reads the URL from grant, and the site address from the lens config, with no hardcoded host
Ping logic checks local /readyz and public /readyz, and reports /fail unless both pass
Tests use real local HTTP listeners for: both pass, local fails, public fails, URL missing
The all-backends rule isn't touched
tasks.instruction: Follow the existing `verb == "install"` flow in console.py and culture_core/persistence.py for unit generation. Keep the check logic in one small function that's testable without systemd.

tasks.summary: culture: log every server link outcome and find why spark's outbound links don't form (#519)
acceptance_criteria: Every link attempt logs success, handshake failure or rejection, with no secrets
Root cause of #519 is written on the issue
spark holds an established link to thor and orin after a server restart, shown by ss and a link-state query
tasks.instruction: Start in agentirc ircd.py connect_to_peer and server_link.py handle, where the task's result is never awaited. agentirc is a sibling repo: the fix may land there first, then a pin bump in culture. See also #510.

tasks.summary: culture: standby rejoins the mesh after a reboot without a person unlocking its keyring (#509)
acceptance_criteria: After a spark2 reboot with no human action, its server holds a link to at least one peer
Link secrets are never written in plain text to a world-readable file, or printed
Docs describe how it's set up and how to rotate it
tasks.instruction: Read #509 first. Moving link secrets from the login keyring to grant, as agent secrets already are, may be simpler than unlocking the keyring. Propose the approach to the owner before building: it touches secret storage.

tasks.summary: irc-lens: trust the public origin and the Worker's credential, so browser POSTs work and direct requests are refused
acceptance_criteria: Files: src/irc_lens/config.py, web/auth.py, web/routes.py (_origin_ok), tests/test_worker_trust.py, docs/deployment-cloudflare-access.md
A POST with Origin equal to the configured public origin passes through the Worker path; any other Origin still gets 403
A request without the Worker's credential is refused when `auth.require_edge_credential` is on, and behaviour is unchanged when it's off
The credential comparison is constant-time, and the secret comes from an env var
tasks.instruction: Take the approach t2's result chose. Default off, so this can ship and deploy before the Worker exists.

tasks.summary: irc-lens: standby mode, for approved users only with account changes and guest mode off
acceptance_criteria: Files: src/irc_lens/config.py, a new web/standby.py, tests/test_standby.py, docs/deployment-cloudflare-access.md
With `standby.enabled`, a guest sign-in gets the outage message and no guest is created
Every route that writes accounts, grants, nicknames, consents or agent credentials refuses with a clear message; a test enumerates them
Approved users sign in and send messages normally, as the server-prefixed nick
The UI shows a banner that says agents and spark media are unavailable
tasks.instruction: List write routes from the stores in access_store.py and guest_store.py, and block at one middleware rather than per route, so a new route can't be missed silently.

tasks.summary: Worker: gate traffic, pin sessions, fail over on repeated /readyz failures, serve the outage page
acceptance_criteria: Files: deploy/chat-edge/worker.js, deploy/chat-edge/outage.html, deploy/chat-edge/worker.test.mjs, deploy/chat-edge/README.md, all in irc-lens
Pure functions, unit tested with no network: pick origin, pin cookie, failure count
A session stays on one origin while it's healthy
Failover needs N consecutive failed checks, so a restart moves no one; returning to spark needs a deliberate config change
Both origins down returns the outage page with status 503
Handler does almost no CPU work: it never parses bodies, and streams SSE through unchanged
tasks.instruction: Keep pure logic separate from fetch so it can be tested with node. Store the active origin in KV, written by a cron check, so requests don't each probe. Deploy using cultureflare's scripts, dry-run first. Owner deploys.

tasks.summary: Provision a separate tunnel for spark2 and an origin hostname for each host
acceptance_criteria: spark and spark2 connect through different tunnel UUIDs, shown by the Cloudflare API
Each origin hostname refuses a request lacking the Worker's credential once t6 is on
The existing chat.culture.dev tunnel route is untouched until t11's rollback path is proven
tasks.instruction: Use cultureflare verbs where they exist. Tunnel tokens go in grant, never in a file in a repo.

tasks.summary: Copy accounts one way from spark to spark2 on a schedule, privately
acceptance_criteria: Files: a new culture_core/cli/shared/console_replica.py and a `culture console replica` verb in culture, with tests
Uses sqlite's backup API, so the copy is consistent while the lens is running
Copy travels only over the tailnet or LAN, lands mode 0600 and is replaced atomically
A copy from a newer schema to an older lens is refused with a clear message
After a copy, an approved person signs in on spark2 with the same role and grants, in a test using two real stores
Retention on the copy matches the original: guest_mode.retention_days, or no guest rows copied
tasks.instruction: Run on spark and push to spark2, so standby needs no way into spark. Guest mode is off on standby: prefer leaving guest and consent rows out, which shrinks the private data on spark2.

tasks.summary: Rollback: remove the Worker in one step and rehearse it
acceptance_criteria: A documented single command removes the Worker route, and traffic returns through the direct tunnel
Rehearsal in production restores signed-in service in under 5 minutes, with the time measured
The runbook says who rotates the Worker's service token, and when it expires
tasks.instruction: Rehearse before any origin lockdown is enforced, so the direct path is known to work.

tasks.summary: Provision spark2 as standby with the supported install verbs
acceptance_criteria: culture console install and culture server install produce running units on spark2
spark2's lens runs in standby mode, reachable only through its tunnel
spark2 has its own health check, or a documented reason it doesn't, and its secrets are in its own grant
tasks.instruction: Keep the same versions on both hosts. spark2's bind address stays on its tailnet or loopback.

tasks.summary: Failover drill in production: measure everything the spec promises
acceptance_criteria: Stopping spark's IRCd alerts the owner within 10 minutes, with the time measured
Signed-in test account reaches spark2 within 5 minutes and sends a real message in a real browser
At least 2 hourly reminder emails arrive while the check is down
Stopping both origins shows the outage page
Restarting the console during a deploy moves no one
History gaps after failover are recorded as observed
Results are filed as evidence, including anything that failed
tasks.instruction: Schedule with the owner, because this is a real interruption. Run it with real browser click-through on every path.

risks.text: History after failover may look incomplete, depending on whether remote-origin messages reach the local history.db
Turnstile through a Worker is unexamined; t13 must exercise a real sign-in with it
Same-zone route, Access on the same hostname, and Worker cron with KV on the Free plan are unverified; t2 and t8 must cover them
Moving link secrets touches secret storage on all four hosts, so t5 needs owner sign-off on its approach
